scenes.text: A multiple -collision question follows what happens after the first impact. A particle might then hit a wall, or a third particle. Deal with each collision separately, because each changes the velocities. Draw a fresh, clearly labelled diagram. Give each new unknown a different name, so you carry the right velocity forward. For a wall, use the rebound information given. The particle's momentum alone is not conserved.

scenes.text: Consider three spheres moving right along a smooth track. A is behind B, and C is further ahead. A catches B. After that impact, A moves more slowly, while B goes ahead and catches C. C moves off and B slows down. A is still behind B. Our question is whether A will catch B again. First picture those two impacts, then we'll calculate what changes.

scenes.text: Ball A, one kilogram, rolling at four metres per second, is behind ball B, two kilograms, rolling at three. Same direction. Will A catch B? Yes, it's faster. So they collide. Ball C, three kilograms, rolls ahead at one metre per second. After A hits B, A moves at two metres per second. After B hits C, C moves at three. Will A and B collide again?

scenes.text: Now collision one. Find B's velocity after A hits it. Right is positive. Let's get drawing. A, one kilogram, four metres per second. B, two kilograms, three metres per second. Afterwards A moves at two metres per second. Call B's new velocity v B. The pair's momentum is conserved because no external force changes its total. Here u means before and v means after. Momentum before equals momentum after. Mass A times u A, plus mass B times u B, equals mass A times v A, plus mass B times v B. the givens on our diagram. A is one kilogram times four, plus B's two kilograms times three, equals A's one kilogram times two, plus B's two kilograms times v B. Ten equals two plus two v B. Subtract two and divide by two, v B is four metres per second. Positive means right. Carry that four forward, not the original three.

Faster left means more negative, because right is positive. With A left of B, A's signed velocity must be greater for the gap to close.
